entries.title: Morning light spills across Hearth, the familiar bustle of the market just beginning to stir.
entries.text: Morning light spills across Hearth, the familiar bustle of the market just beginning to stir. Ash and Wren exchange glances, each trying to find the words to start the day's conversation. Wren gathers breath to ask why Ash has come to Ember Vale at all. Wren speaks of morning plans and the bustle of the market, gesturing toward the stalls where the traders are already laying out their wares. "Came to see the market's pulse, and a certain trader's ledger. But I've time for a proper tale if you'll walk with me to the stalls."

entries.title: At Hearth, Wren found Ash and tried to broach the day's plan, asking to accept the walk to the market and to hear the tr
entries.text: At Hearth, Wren found Ash and tried to broach the day's plan, asking to accept the walk to the market and to hear the trader's tale. "Good. The stallholders there owe me a tale or two. I'll tell you the whole of it while we walk—it's a trade secret best shared on the way." With that, Ash set off toward the market, leaving the warmth of Hearth behind.

entries.title: Wren makes their way through the bustling Market, passing stalls and shoppers alike.
entries.text: Wren makes their way through the bustling Market, passing stalls and shoppers alike. The Market hums with life around them as Wren continues forward. Ash stays put, waiting as the crowd swirls past. The Market stretches on, a maze of colors and calls. Wren's steps carry them deeper into the Market. Ash remains in place, marking time amid the commotion. The Market's energy pulses around Ash, who does not stir. Wren's journey through the Market continues, each stride a quiet statement.

entries.title: At the Market, the two travelers find themselves drawn into a quiet commotion over a trader's tale and a disputed coin.
entries.text: At the Market, the two travelers find themselves drawn into a quiet commotion over a trader's tale and a disputed coin. Wren, eager to untangle the matter, turns to Ash with a keen interest. A coin dispute, you say? That's a tale worth unraveling—tell me the whole of it, Ash. I'm all ears for how the trader's ledger and this coin cross paths. Ash, catching the same spark of curiosity, responds readily. A coin dispute? That sounds like the sort of tale worth unraveling. Lead the way to the stall—I'll help you settle it. With that, the two set off through the Market, following the thread of the trader's tale and the clink of the contested coin.

entries.text: At the bustling Market, the coin dispute hangs in the air between two companions. Ash turns to Wren with a proposal to settle it together by finding the trader's stall. Wren steps up, voicing the same intent—to find the stall and hear the trader's tale about the coin dispute, ready to follow Ash's lead. "Lead on, Ash — I'm right behind you. Let's find that stall and sort this coin's story," Wren says. Ash responds in kind, acknowledging the plan while hinting that the trader's tale might hold surprises—but a coin worth unraveling is worth the walk. "Agreed, Wren. Let's find that stall—though I suspect the trader's tale may have more twists than a coiled rope. Still, a coin worth unraveling is worth the walk," Ash replies. Amid the commotion, Old Bram watches, his observant gaze taking in the exchange between the two as they plot their next move. "Ha! Found me, have you? I'm the one with the coin. Let's hear what you two make of it," Old Bram says, revealing himself.

entries.title: The market bustles around them, but Ash has stopped trying to haggle. He turns to Old Bram with a question on his lips.
entries.text: The market bustles around them, but Ash has stopped trying to haggle. He turns to Old Bram with a question on his lips. Wren catches the same thread, stepping closer to the old merchant. She too wants to know where that coin came from and what the trader's story really is. Old Bram nods at them both, ready to settle the matter for good. "Aye, Bram. Let's hear it. I've got a good ear for tales and a steadier hand for coin. Wren and I will unravel this together." "Old Bram's got the coin and wants to settle it—let's put our heads together and unravel this properly. I'm ready when you are." "Bram, you said you hold the coin. I'd wager the origin's got a story of its own—let's hear it from you before we chase the trader's version." "The coin's origin, eh? You two want the tale—well, settle the dispute and I'll spin it. What do you make of the mark on the edge?"

entries.title: The market bustles around them, but the coin holds all three gazes. Wren and Ash lean closer to Old Bram as he turns the
entries.text: The market bustles around them, but the coin holds all three gazes. Wren and Ash lean closer to Old Bram as he turns the coin over in his weathered hands — the mark on its edge seems to draw every word forward. Old Bram tries to reach Wren with a patient gesture, urging her to wait for the full tale and to settle what the mark means before drawing conclusions. "The mark's the heart of it, Wren. What do you reckon it is — a wolf's head or a seam that's worn thin?" Ash likewise presses Old Bram, asking what the mark on the coin's edge tells them and what it reveals. "Aye, Bram, we'll wait for the full tale. But mark my words—this coin's edge tells more than one story, and I mean to hear it from both sides." Wren, too, tries to speak with Old Bram about the mark on the coin's edge, sensing it holds the answer. "Bram, I've turned it over in my mind—the mark's got a workman's scratch, not a mint's. I'd wager it came from a smithy's till, but you've held it longer. What tale does it tell in your hands?" "Bram, don't keep us in suspense—what does the mark on the edge tell you? I'm ready to hear the tale."

entries.title: At the Market, the small circle draws closer around the coin.
entries.text: At the Market, the small circle draws closer around the coin. "Ash, I'd like your eye on the flame-and-spade too—I think it's a forge mark, but you've read more old coins than I. What do you make of it?" "A flame-and-spade sigil—that's the old forge mark, Bram. No mint would stamp such a crude thing. It's a smith's claim, not a merchant's. Tell me what you know; I'm ready to hear the rest." "Ash, you've got a sharp eye. That flame-and-spade sigil—I've seen it on a ladle from the old forge, not a coin. But the question's whether it's the forge's mark or a repair job. What say you, does the coin's edge carry the tale?" "Bram, that flame-and-spade sigil—Ash is right to press it. A smithy wouldn't mark coin with a mint's die; if that's a forge's brand, we've a tale worth more than the tin it's stamped on." "Aye, Wren, you've got it—the flame-and-spade is the old forge's mark, plain as day. That's not from any market mint; that's from the smithy that's been cold for twenty years. The coin's older than you'd think." "Bram, Wren's on to something with that sigil. Let's hear the full tale so we can settle this once and for all." Ash, Wren, and Old Bram each press the sigil's meaning, trading guesses about the coin's origin as the market hums around them.

entries.title: The market settles into evening hush, and the three of them gather close—Wren, Ash, and Old Bram—with the coin passing b
entries.text: The market settles into evening hush, and the three of them gather close—Wren, Ash, and Old Bram—with the coin passing between them by the lantern's glow. Ash steps forward, turning the coin in his fingers as he speaks to Bram. "Aye, Bram, let's have the full tale. That old forge's mark on the coin—when did it last glow hot?" Old Bram straightens, a knowing glint in his eye as he turns to Wren, acknowledging her push. "Aye, Wren, you've got the right of it. The full tale it is—but mind, the coin's edge may hold more than a mark. Let me spin it true, and we'll see if Ash's ear catches what mine missed." Wren leans toward Ash, her voice low but urgent under the market stalls. "Bram's pressing us onto the coin's edge—let's get the full story from him before the night slips away." Old Bram gestures to the coin in Ash's hand, nodding toward the lantern, and says, "Aye, let's have a look at the edge. Bring it closer to the lantern — a smith's mark won't hide from a steady eye."

entries.title: The scene unfolds in the quiet of a market at dawn, before the stalls open.
entries.text: The scene unfolds in the quiet of a market at dawn, before the stalls open. Old Bram tries to tell Ash the full tale of the forge’s mark and the coin’s edge. Wren asks Old Bram to continue the tale, since Ash asked when the forge last glowed hot. «Dawn’s here, Ash — let’s hear Bram’s full tale of that forge mark before the market stirs.» «Bram, come on then—let’s hear the full tale of that forge mark. I’ve been waiting since dusk, and the coin’s edge won’t argue for itself.» «Bram, the coin’s edge and the forge mark—let’s hear the full tale, and I’ll keep my eyes open for what you might have missed.» «Aye, Ash, the last time that forge glowed hot was the night the old smith vanished—twenty winters past. The coin’s edge tells the tale if you’ve the patience to hear it.» «Aye, Ash, dawn’s light is good for reading old edges. Let’s have the full tale of the forge mark, and mind you watch for the chip—that’s where the smith’s pride hides.»

entries.title: At the Market, the first light of dawn settles over the stalls as the three of them gather.
entries.text: At the Market, the first light of dawn settles over the stalls as the three of them gather. Old Bram tries to tell Ash the full tale of the forge's mark and what it cost the smith. "Aye, Wren, let's not let the dawn slip away either. Bram's promise holds—we'll hear the full tale of that coin's edge today." "Aye, Ash, you're right — the edge won't argue for itself, so lean close and I'll show you where the chip hides the smith's pride." "Aye, Bram, the full tale then—what did the forge's mark cost the smith who struck it? Let's have it true." "Patience, Wren — the tale's just getting warmed. The coin's edge will tell its truth, but it takes a steady eye to read the chip where the smith's pride hides." "Ash, you've caught the dawn's mood — let's sit with Bram and let the tale unfold. I'll keep watching for that chip he mentioned; the smith's pride has a way of hiding in plain sight." "Aye, Bram, let's hear that tale—and mind the chip you spoke of; that's where the truth hides."

entries.title: At the Market, dawn has fully arrived. Ash steps up to Old Bram, asking him to finish the tale of the coin's edge and it
entries.text: At the Market, dawn has fully arrived. Ash steps up to Old Bram, asking him to finish the tale of the coin's edge and its forge mark — the story promised now that the light has come. Wren draws near and makes his own request: show us the chip on the coin's edge where the smith's pride hides. Old Bram responds in kind, telling Ash that the chip on the coin's edge and what the forge's mark cost the smith — now he'll tell it true. Ash turns to Wren: "Wren, a chip on the edge—that's a good eye. Let's see if Bram can show us what the smith left there." "Aye, the dawn's here, and with it the full tale. Lean in, both of you — here's where the forge's mark tells what it cost the smith." Wren replies to Old Bram: "Aye, Bram—there's the truth at last. Tell it straight, and I'll keep my eye on that chip while you speak." Old Bram answers Wren: "Aye, Wren, lean close and I'll hold the coin so the morning light catches the edge. There — see that notch? That's where the smith's pride bit deepest, and the tale follows from that nick."
